content.title: Hawks vs. Knicks Prediction, NBA Playoff Picks, Spread – 4/20/26
content.text: The Atlanta Hawks vs. New York Knicks NBA Playoff game is set to tip off at 8:00 p.m. ET on Monday, April 20, with the Knicks entering as 4.5-point favorites on the spread, via PrizePicks.Atlanta and New York add another chapter to their rivalry with what should be an entertaining first-round playoff matchup. The Knicks took the lead late in the first quarter in Game 1 and never relinquished it, winning (and covering) 113-102.Below, we'll break down our Hawks vs. Knicks prediction and picks for Monday’s game, including the spread, over/under, and key player picks for PrizePicks.Make your picks for Hawks vs. Knicks on PrizePicks now.Hawks vs. Knicks Prediction, Spread, Over/Under – Monday, April 20Atlanta has shed the weight of its past by trading away former face of the franchise, PG Trae Young. They're embracing a youth movement, highlighted by PF Jalen Johnson and SG Nickeil Alexander-Walker.Game 1 was a tough one for NAW, as he shot 6-for-17 from the field, finishing with just 17 points. He'll have to be better if the Hawks hope to win Game 2 and steal a game in New York. The Knicks had a fantastic regular season and rolled that momentum straight into the postseason. They finished the campaign with two more wins than last year but still occupy the same seed. After reaching the Eastern Conference Finals in 2025, New York looks to build on that and return to the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999.It was a quality team effort from the Knicks in Game 1, but they may like PG Jalen Brunson to be more efficient than the 9-for-22 he shot. On the road, the Knicks are 15-26 (36.6%) ATS, tied for the worst road cover record. Fortunately for them, tonight’s game is at Madison Square Garden.The Knicks possess a sizeable advantage on the glass over Atlanta, sitting fifth in rebounding percentage (52.2%) to the Hawks' 49.5% mark (17th). The Hawks' defense is opportunistic, ranking fourth in points scored off turnovers at 17.4%. That could be tough to replicate against a Knicks squad that gives up the second-fewest steals each night (7.3). New York owned the 10th-best regular-season free throw percentage (79.2%), while the Hawks ranked 20th (77.4%). The Knicks shot 25-for-30 from the line in Game 1, meanwhile Atlanta went 12-for-19.
